scope.subject: Flink mechanisms applicable to the next native streaming epoch

mandatory_invariants: A terminal platform acceptance atomically binds the input coordinate, output outcome, authoritative managed-state mutation, completion receipt, and consumer progress.
If durable progress through input 200 is accepted, replacement execution admits business input 201; it does not re-enter Python business calls 101 through 200.
A snapshot may accelerate state materialization, rescaling, backup, or garbage collection, but it is never the sole authority for accepted business progress.
Platform-managed output, cursor, and state recovery does not imply exactly-once PostgreSQL, HTTP, filesystem, or other client effects; external-effect idempotency remains client-owned.
A broker product is not a prerequisite. A source must instead provide a native durable partition log or an explicit versioned split, offset, rewind, and retention contract.
Lease expiry, heartbeat loss, or network timeout is not proof of process death for cross-host replacement.
Opaque unjournaled Python, closure, global, or process-local state is unsupported by the mandatory recovery contract unless a different replay contract is explicitly approved.

terminal_outcome_correction.decision: Future multi-input and join turns that may emit zero or one output require an explicit tagged NO_OUTPUT outcome or an equivalently explicit new cardinality-0..1 protocol.
constraints: Absence of output must not be inferred from Python None because None is a legitimate JSON value.
An ordinary Python return remains a value-bearing language outcome and must not be silently reinterpreted as no output.
The existing internal YIELD/RETURN wire representation is not, by itself, approval for the future public join contract.
Exact SDK spelling and migration behavior remain undecided and unimplemented.

supported_classes.name: INLINE_TURN_STATE
supported_classes.contract: The authoritative state postimage or bounded mutation set commits in the terminal transaction.

supported_classes.name: JOURNALED_TURN_STATE_WITH_SNAPSHOTS
supported_classes.contract: A versioned platform mutation batch commits in the terminal transaction; snapshots are derived caches reconstructed without invoking user task code.

state_authority.rejected_inference: A checkpoint-managed local state snapshot does not authorize replay of already completed Python business inputs.
materialization_replay: Load a complete compatible snapshot at or before the accepted frontier.
Apply the verified contiguous platform mutation batches in durable apply-ordinal order.
Do not call the task function, emit output, advance an already advanced cursor, or repeat client effects.
If the chain is missing, corrupt, incompatible, or cannot reach the accepted frontier, fail closed or select another verified materialization; never rewind completed business progress.
terminal_receipt_bindings: input coordinate and tagged input port
tagged output outcome and immutable output identity when present

task_run_identity_refinement.reason: The epoch-1 bounded profile used one TaskRun per logical source or operator. Physical partition parallelism requires a new explicit agreement rather than a silent reinterpretation.
proposal: A logical operator has a stable operator UID.
A physical subtask identity is bound to FlowRun, graph revision, operator UID, assignment epoch, and subtask index.
Each physical subtask is one ordinary TaskRun that processes many records and key groups.
Retry or infrastructure replacement preserves that TaskRun identity and increments its attempt or run_count.
A planned rescale creates a bounded new subtask TaskRun set only at a completed state-transfer cut.
task_run_identity_refinement.complexity: O(operators times parallelism times assignment epochs), never O(documents)
task_run_identity_refinement.rejected_alternative: Concurrent physical workers hidden under one jointly owned TaskRun would make Prefect lifecycle ownership and stale-writer fencing ambiguous.

flink_mechanisms_to_adapt: Static graph and revision identity, source splits, operator subtasks, and stable key groups decoupled from current parallelism.
DATA and checkpoint barriers ordered in each partition log, multi-input barrier alignment, and complete-only snapshot selection.
Backpressure propagated from downstream capacity, with separate busy, idle, and backpressured observations.
Per-partition watermarks, minimum-over-active-input advancement, explicit idleness, watermark alignment, and durable timer state.
Recovery-region reasoning that expands upstream when a required retained partition is unavailable and includes affected consumers when state or outputs roll back.
flink_mechanisms_not_to_copy_directly: Periodic checkpoint plus source replay as the sole recovery authority.
A second JobManager or scheduler beside Prefect server, FlowRun, TaskRun, and worker lifecycle authority.
Unaligned checkpoints before durable channel-state identity and measured alignment pressure justify them.
Exactly-once claims for arbitrary Python client effects.
Java object hashCode or Python hash as a cross-process partition identity.
Processing-time TTL as correctness authority for event-time join cleanup.

current_native_blockers.finding: The accepted public profile is finite bounded-linear-v1, has one stream input, one output cardinality, and a finite positioned source.
The server seals exactly one ordered source-to-operator linear manifest.
Source progress is one scalar contiguous position and the current consumer binding represents one TaskRun input; multi-input ports and partition vectors need new identities.
Capacity is a hard bounded refusal and retained record and byte counts grow until release; continuous input requires awaitable credit plus online segment retention.
The accepted worker profile is bounded-linear-v1 with same-host linux-local-pidfd-v1 recovery, not partitioned cross-host recovery.

candidate_adr_boundaries.topic: Native distributed-stream execution model and authority boundaries
Partitioned channels, key groups, physical subtasks, and fan-out
Multi-input mailbox turns, journaled state authority, joins, and consistent barrier cuts
Continuous split sources, event time, watermarks, timers, and cleanup
Durable credits, online retention, fairness, and overload policy
Recovery regions, subordinate fencing, and verified cross-host replacement
Rescaling, state compatibility, load, chaos, and production acceptance

required_counterexamples_and_controls: Snapshot 100, durable cursor 200, and missing or corrupt mutation 151 must refuse activation rather than invoke business calls 151 through 200.
A noncommutative join must rebuild state in persisted mailbox apply-ordinal order, not independent per-input sequence order.
A state-only terminal turn must remain distinguishable from an output whose JSON value is null.
Lost acknowledgement after terminal commit must discover the receipt and skip user-code re-entry.
Timer registration, cancellation, and firing identities must survive cache reconstruction without duplicate callbacks.
Snapshot garbage collection must refuse incomplete, incompatible, corrupt, or still-pinned materializations.
A lagging branch must pin required segments and return durable capacity without advancing another consumer's cursor.
An old cross-host worker that may still be alive must block takeover; only a profile-specific verified death witness may authorize a generation change.

cases: Commit business turns 1 through 200 as immutable terminal receipts and state mutation batches.
Rebuild a fresh cache from the snapshot and platform batches 101 through 200 without incrementing the business-call or external-effect counters.
Verify immutable output and cursor identities remain through 200 and the next business admission is 201.
Lose the process before and after mutation-batch and snapshot commits.
Delete or corrupt batch 151 and verify fail-closed recovery without business re-entry.
first_probe.evidence_limit: This probe earns zero native readiness. Native acceptance requires ordinary Prefect TaskRuns, real HTTP and PostgreSQL transactions, process loss, and the relevant cross-host profile.

exploratory_master_source.note: These files corroborated mechanisms during discussion. Normative ADR code citations require a release-2.3.0 commit or tag resolved separately.

acceptance_boundary: No theory or ADR in this discussion is accepted by documentation or prototype evidence alone. Historical accepted evidence remains intact; all new ADRs remain planning or progress until their native implementation and named acceptance controls pass.
